subtype: Approach: clarify own role and possible involvement [Thinking]
passage:
Rehana, you asked what kept me awake, and it was not the numbers. It was that I had signed off the earlier reports myself. I kept asking, if something was wrong in those, am I part of it? Did I miss it, or did I look away? Those are different questions, and I needed to answer them honestly before I pointed at anybody else.

So I pulled out my old sign-offs and checked what I had actually seen at the time. Then I booked an hour with a lawyer to ask how to disclose my own part properly. I'm Vandana, and I'll be honest, that hour was uncomfortable. But when I wrote my report, my own role was in the first paragraph, and nothing could surprise me later.

qa.q: What did Vandana pull out to check before writing the report?
qa.a: Vandana pulled out the old sign-offs to check what had been seen at the time.

qa.q: What was Vandana worried about when thinking of the earlier reports?
qa.a: Vandana worried about being part of the problem, wondering whether something had been missed or overlooked.

qa.q: What could Vandana do if the lawyer's hour raised new worries, and why?
qa.a: Vandana could write down the questions and raise them with the compliance channel or a supervisor, because being upfront early avoids bigger surprises later.

qa.q: How might Rehana, who asked the question, see Vandana looking at Vandana's own role first?
qa.a: Rehana may admire the honesty, since starting with a personal check makes the later report more credible.

grounding: The auditor asks whether earlier sign-offs make them part of the issue and checks how to disclose it, valuing honest reflection.
